title_en: China Everbright Bank v. Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding & Decoration Factory, Agricultural Bank of China Baotou Qingshan District Sub-branch, and Baotou Qingshan District People's Government Ziyou Road Sub-district Office — tort dispute
full_text_en:
China Everbright Bank v. Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding and Decoration Factory, China Agricultural Bank Baotou Qingshan District Sub-branch, and Ziyou Road Office of the People's Government of Qingshan District, Baotou City — dispute over tort

Ruling Summary

The so-called post-event mortgage generally refers to a situation where a debtor has multiple ordinary creditors and, when repaying debts, maliciously colludes with one of the creditors to mortgage all or part of its property to that creditor. The creation of such a post-event mortgage typically occurs when the debtor has already fallen into a payment crisis, is on the verge of bankruptcy, and its property is insufficient to satisfy all debts. The creation of a post-event mortgage inevitably leads to a reduction or loss of its ability to perform other debts, thereby damaging the legitimate interests of other creditors. Therefore, such a post-event mortgage should be deemed invalid, and the mortgagee has no priority right to receive payment from the proceeds obtained from exercising the mortgage; if the proceeds have already been obtained, they shall be returned in accordance with the law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 135

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Everbright Bank, domiciled at: Everbright Tower, No. 6 Fuxingmenwai Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Tang Shuangning, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Dequan, Staff Member of Inner Mongolia Asset Management Department of China Everbright Bank.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaoxia, Lawyer of Beijing Shuangli Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding and Decoration Factory, domiciled at: No. 6 Minzhu Road, Qingshan District, Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Fu Zhebiao, Factory Director.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): China Agricultural Bank Baotou Qingshan District Sub-branch, domiciled at: No. 206 Kexue Road, Qingshan District, Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Person in Charge: Chen Yonghe, Sub-branch President.

Agent ad litem: Xu Bin, Staff Member of China Agricultural Bank Baotou Branch.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Ziyou Road Office of the People's Government of Qingshan District, Baotou City, domiciled at: Block No. 5, Ziyou Road, Qingshan District, Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Person in Charge: Dong Xianyu, Secretary of the Party Working Committee of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jing, Deputy Director of the Office.

Appellant China Everbright Bank (hereinafter referred to as Everbright Bank) filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2007) Nei Min Er Chu Zi No. 21 of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court regarding a tort dispute with Appellees Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding and Decoration Factory (hereinafter referred to as Huada Decoration Factory), China Agricultural Bank Baotou Qingshan District Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch), and Ziyou Road Office of the People's Government of Qingshan District, Baotou City (hereinafter referred to as Ziyou Road Office). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Adjudicator Jin Jianfeng as the presiding judge, and Acting Adjudicators Yin Yuan and Pan Yongfeng, with Clerk Bai Xue serving as the record keeper. This case is now concluded.

The First Instance of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court found the following facts: Huada Decoration Factory failed to repay its loan to Everbright Bank when due. In 2004, Everbright Bank filed a lawsuit with the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court requesting Huada Decoration Factory to repay the matured debt. The creditor's rights formed by Everbright Bank's loan to Huada Decoration Factory were confirmed in the civil judgment (2004) Nei Min Er Chu Zi No. 4. Thereafter, Everbright Bank applied for enforcement. However, because Huada Decoration Factory had no other property aside from the mortgaged factory buildings and land, Everbright Bank's creditor's rights were not satisfied. In 2004, on the grounds of malicious collusion harming the interests of other creditors, Everbright Bank filed a lawsuit with the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court, requesting confirmation that the mortgage contract was invalid and that the mortgaged property be restored to its unmortgaged state. The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48, which confirmed that the mortgage contract signed between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch was invalid, and rejected Everbright Bank's claim to restore the mortgaged property to its unmortgaged state. On July 25, 2007, Everbright Bank filed a lawsuit with the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court against Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch as defendants; on January 10, 2008, Everbright Bank applied to add Ziyou Road Office as a defendant. Everbright Bank's claims were: 1. Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch shall be jointly and severally liable for compensating Everbright Bank's losses of RMB 25,606,683.28 (including USD principal of USD 588,149.69, interest of USD 2,649,600.62; RMB principal of RMB 526,778.05, interest of RMB 473,002.87; USD conversion rate 7.6); 2. Ziyou Road Office shall bear the liquidation responsibility for Huada Decoration Factory and assume civil liability with the liquidation assets; 3. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne jointly by Huada Decoration Factory, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch, and Ziyou Road Office.

The first instance judgment of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court held that the reason the court's civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48 confirmed the invalidity of the mortgage was that the debtor, after falling into a payment crisis, mortgaged all of its effective assets to one creditor, thereby causing other ordinary creditors to lose the opportunity for satisfaction. Based on the subjective malice present in this aspect, the court found that the post-event mortgage between the parties was invalid. However, the malicious mortgage parties infringed upon the opportunity of other ordinary creditors to obtain satisfaction, and there was no direct causal relationship between this and the failure to repay the loan under the loan contract with Everbright Bank. Huada Decoration Factory had already been ordered by a legally effective judgment of the court to assume contractual repayment liability; it should not undertake tort liability in this case. Therefore, in this case, Everbright Bank's request that Ziyou Road Office, based on the premise of Huada Decoration Factory's tort liability, assume the liquidation responsibility as the supervising unit and bear liability with the liquidation assets, lacked the prerequisite conditions. In accordance with Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC and Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled: Reject Everbright Bank's claims. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 169,657.20 shall be borne by Everbright Bank.

Everbright Bank, dissatisfied with the aforementioned civil judgment of the first instance court, filed an appeal with this Court, stating: The first instance judgment made erroneous findings of fact. The first instance judgment failed to find the fact that Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch fabricated creditor's rights and created a mortgage; the facts of this case and the first instance court's civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48 did not find the mortgage contract invalid solely based on the confirmation of a post-event mortgage. The disputed mortgage loan contracts for RMB 1.69 million and RMB 270,000 were not actually performed; they were fabricated creditor's rights and debts. Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory created the mortgage under the premise of fabricated creditor's rights and debts; the first instance court's determination that the mortgage between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch constituted a post-event mortgage lacked factual basis. The malicious collusion between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch in fabricating creditor's rights, creating a mortgage, and disposing of the mortgaged property caused Huada Decoration Factory to lose essential means of production, leading to its complete loss of debt repayment ability, thereby constituting infringement upon Everbright Bank's creditor's rights. There is a causal relationship between the parties' actions and Everbright Bank's losses, which resulted in the complete inability to realize Everbright Bank's creditor's rights. Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch shall be jointly and severally liable for the full loss of Everbright Bank's creditor's rights. Request the second instance to set aside the first instance judgment and rule in favor of its first instance claims.

Appellee Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch responded in its defense: (1) Everbright Bank's filing of this lawsuit violates both the procedural principle of res judicata and the mandatory legal provisions regarding the concurrence of breach of contract and tort actions. The current legal provisions in China do not apply tort actions to the protection of ordinary contract creditor's rights; Everbright Bank's tort action lacks legal basis. (2) The act of a creditor agreeing with the debtor to dispose of the debtor's property for the purpose of realizing the creditor's rights is lawful and does not constitute a tort. In the legal relationship of a mortgage loan, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch was both the mortgagee and the creditor. Even if the mortgage contract is found invalid and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch no longer has the priority right of a mortgagee, it remains an ordinary bank creditor. The act of Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch agreeing with Huada Decoration Factory to dispose of property for realizing the creditor's rights does not violate any prohibitive legal provisions, does not constitute a tort, and is lawful and valid and should be protected by law. (3) Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory merely created a post-event mortgage to secure the pre-existing debt, and did not fabricate any creditor's rights and debts. In this case, to secure the pre-existing loan debt of RMB 1.494 million, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory signed two mortgage loan contracts with the loan purpose listed as "settling debts", which were handled in accordance with legal provisions and the requirements of the superior bank that buildings and land use rights be mortgaged simultaneously, and they completed the mortgage registration procedures. The first instance court did not confirm in its civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48 the fact of fabricated creditor's rights and debts as alleged by Everbright Bank. (4) There is no causal relationship between the failure to realize Everbright Bank's loan creditor's rights and the creation of the mortgage by Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch. According to legal provisions, when a mortgage is created and the mortgage is enforced, the mortgagee only has a priority right to repayment; the four powers of ownership of the mortgaged property are not affected in any way, and it certainly does not affect the business operations of the mortgagor. Huada Decoration Factory had completely ceased production in 1998; setting up the mortgage in 1999 could not have affected the production and operation of a factory that had already been closed for one year. In 2003, to solve the problem of five years of unpaid wages for Huada Decoration Factory employees, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory negotiated the transfer of the real estate for RMB 2.25 million, of which RMB 1 million was used for employee living expenses and RMB 1.25 million to repay Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch's loan. The reason Everbright Bank's loan creditor's rights could not be realized was due to Huada Decoration Factory's poor business management, consecutive years of losses, severe insolvency, and complete cessation of production and business operations, which had nothing to do with Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch's act of realizing its creditor's rights. Request the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

Appellee Huada Decoration Factory did not submit a written defense.

Appellee Ziyou Road Office did not submit a written defense. At the second instance trial during cross-examination, it orally defended that Huada Decoration Factory is a collectively-owned enterprise, currently in a state of automatic dissolution. After being placed under the supervision of Ziyou Road Office, Ziyou Road Office is only responsible for resolving employees' insurance issues; it is not responsible for other matters. The property liquidation of a collectively-owned enterprise should be carried out by the employees' congress. It requests the original judgment be affirmed.

The second instance of this Court found that the following facts were determined in the civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48 of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court:

In January 1989, the former Inner Mongolia Branch of the China Investment Bank extended a World Bank on-lending loan of USD 570,680 and RMB 919,280 to the former Baotou No. 4 Woodenware Factory. Later, the debtor was changed to Huada Decoration Factory, which undertook to repay the principal and interest by September 20, 1999. In March 1999, the creditor was changed to Everbright Bank. As of September 2003, Huada Decoration Factory still owed Everbright Bank foreign exchange loan principal and interest of USD 2,332,778.39 and RMB loan principal and interest of RMB 1,470,093.21.

On September 30, 1999, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory signed a mortgage loan contract, stipulating a loan amount of RMB 1.69 million, loan purpose as "settling debts", loan term from September 30, 1999 to September 29, 2000, loan interest rate at 5.85 per mille per month, mortgaged property being a building with an appraised value of RMB 2.46 million. On the same day, the parties signed a real estate mortgage contract, and on October 6 of the same year, they completed the building mortgage registration. On October 18 of the same year, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory signed another mortgage loan contract, stipulating a loan amount of RMB 270,000, loan purpose as "settling debts", loan term from October 18, 1999 to October 17, 2000, loan interest rate at 5.85 per mille per month, mortgaged property being land with an appraised value of RMB 660,000, land type as allocated state-owned land use right. This mortgage was registered.

Additionally, a loan receipt of Agricultural Bank of China showed that Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch extended a short-term loan of RMB 1.494 million to Huada Decoration Factory, with a loan term from November 1, 1999 to December 20, 1999, loan purpose as "settling debts", loan interest rate at 5.952 per mille per month. The loan receipt indicated repayment of principal of RMB 1 million on June 10, 2003, and repayment of principal of RMB 250,000 on July 10, 2003.

On November 7, 2002, for the purpose of recovering the loan, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch signed a "Property Transfer Agreement" with Huada Decoration Factory and Baotou Zhengye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengye Company), intending to transfer all mortgaged buildings and land use rights to Zhengye Company. On February 25, 2003, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch, Huada Decoration Factory, and Baotou Land Reserve Center signed a "Land Use Right Acquisition Contract", stipulating that the Baotou Land Reserve Center would acquire the mortgaged state-owned land use right of Huada Decoration Factory, and it would be listed for trading in April of the same year. Zhengye Company participated in the bidding and obtained the land use right and the buildings attached to the land, and signed a listing transaction confirmation on April 30. Zhengye Company paid RMB 2.809 million. On September 26 of the same year, the Baotou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources issued the "State-owned Land Use Right Certificate" for the above-listed land to Zhengye Company. Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch recovered loans of RMB 1 million and RMB 250,000 from Huada Decoration Factory on June 10 and July 10, 2003, respectively.

On November 10, 2000, after learning that Huada Decoration Factory had mortgaged its buildings and land to Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch, Everbright Bank sent a letter to the People's Government of Qingshan District, Baotou City, concerning the further implementation of Huada Decoration Factory's financial creditor's rights, requesting the Qingshan District People's Government to implement its creditor's rights in accordance with the State Council's "Notice on Several Opinions on Strengthening the Management of Foreign Government Loans" and the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on the Validity of a Debtor Mortgaging All Its Property to One of Its Multiple Creditors." On July 22, 2003, the Qingshan District People's Government issued a report on this issue, which mentioned that the legal representative of Huada Decoration Factory, Fu Zhebiao, had been removed from the factory director position by the Qingshan District Commission for Discipline Inspection and Supervision Bureau in 2001, and the Party branch secretary temporarily took charge. Without the knowledge of the Qingshan District People's Government, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and the former enterprise head Fu Zhebiao privately reached an agreement, and in 2002, they entrusted the Baotou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources Land Reserve Center to auction Huada Decoration Factory's buildings and land, with the buyer being Zhengye Company. In May 2003, after the Qingshan District People's Government discovered this, it immediately intervened and made multiple attempts to coordinate with the Baotou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Zhengye Company, requesting a halt to the relevant land transfer procedures, but all were to no avail.

The civil judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48 of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court held that: The mortgage loan contracts for RMB 1.69 million and RMB 270,000 signed between Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory were not actually performed in terms of the loans they secured; the purpose of signing the contracts was to create a mortgage for pre-existing debts. Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch claimed that the pre-existing debt of RMB 1.494 million consisted of a loan of RMB 1.324 million on June 25, 1998, and a loan of RMB 170,000 on September 28, 1999. However, the two loans differed in loan time, term, purpose, interest rate, etc. The loan receipts for these two loans on their face indicated that they had been repaid, with repayment dates both on November 3, 1999, bearing the same transfer seal as the receipt for RMB 1.494 million. The purpose of the RMB 1.494 million loan was also "settling debts". It could be seen that Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch consolidated the pre-existing debts into one loan receipt of RMB 1.494 million. Therefore, by signing the mortgage loan contracts and the real estate mortgage contract, Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory caused all of Huada Decoration Factory's effective assets to be mortgaged for the Agricultural Bank loan. The parties had subjective malice, and this act harmed the interests of other creditors. Thus, the real estate mortgage between Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory was invalid; Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch had no priority right to repayment from the proceeds obtained from exercising the mortgage, and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch should return those proceeds to Huada Decoration Factory. The respective creditor's rights of Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch and Everbright Bank could be resolved through separate lawsuits. Since Everbright Bank did not raise a claim to confirm the invalidity of the real estate transfer between Huada Decoration Factory and Zhengye Company, and Zhengye Company had already become the actual owner and user of the real estate through the corresponding procedures, Everbright Bank's request to restore the mortgaged property to its unmortgaged state lacked legal support.

The second instance additionally found: The enterprise type of Huada Decoration Factory was collective ownership, originally under the jurisdiction of the Baotou Qingshan District Economic and Trade Bureau. In July 2002, in accordance with the principle of territorial management, Huada Decoration Factory was placed under the supervision of Ziyou Road Office. On July 7, 2004, Huada Decoration Factory's business license was revoked by the industrial and commercial administration authorities.

Apart from the above facts, this Court confirms the facts found by the first instance court.

This Court holds that the focal issues in dispute among the parties in the second instance are whether Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank Qingshan Sub-branch shall bear tort liability for Everbright Bank's losses, and whether Ziyou Road Office shall conduct liquidation of Huada Decoration Factory and assume civil liability with the liquidation assets.

Regarding the ground of appeal raised by China Everbright Bank that Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch had infringed its rights and should compensate for its loss of creditor's rights, Everbright Bank argued that the facts found by the original trial court were erroneous, that Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch had created a fictitious creditor's right and set up a mortgage, and that there was no factual basis for finding that the mortgage between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch was an ex post facto mortgage. This Court holds that the finding that the mortgage between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch was an ex post facto mortgage was a fact found and determined by the original trial court in Civil Judgment (2005) Nei Min Er Zhong Zi No. 48, which has become legally effective. Everbright Bank did not provide new evidence in this case, that is, there is no evidence proving its allegation that the creditor's right between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch was fictitious. The original trial court's confirmation of the facts of this case based on an effective legal instrument was not improper. Everbright Bank argued that Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch had maliciously colluded to create a fictitious creditor's right, set up a mortgage, and dispose of the mortgaged property, and that there was a causal relationship with Everbright Bank's loss, so they should bear joint and several liability for compensation for the entire loss of its creditor's rights. As stated above, the mortgage between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch was an ex post facto mortgage. So-called ex post facto mortgage generally refers to a situation where a debtor has multiple ordinary creditors, and when settling debts, the debtor maliciously colludes with one of the creditors to mortgage all or part of its property to that creditor, thereby losing the ability to perform other debts and harming the lawful rights and interests of other creditors. Typically, the malicious collusion between a debtor and one of its creditors to create an ex post facto mortgage occurs when the debtor has already fallen into a payment crisis, i.e., the debtor is nearing bankruptcy and its property is insufficient to pay off all debts. After such mortgage is confirmed invalid, the legal consequence is that the mortgagee has no priority right to be compensated from the proceeds obtained through exercising the mortgage; if such proceeds have already been obtained, they shall be returned according to law. Based on the facts found in this case, Everbright Bank had already initiated two lawsuits in the original trial court for the protection of its own creditor's rights: a dispute over a loan contract and a dispute over confirming the invalidity of the mortgage contract. The original trial court, based on the facts found, had rendered judgments respectively, ordering Huada Decoration Factory to bear liability for breach of contract for repayment under the loan contract and confirming that the mortgage contract between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch was invalid. Therefore, the original trial court's finding in this case that Huada Decoration Factory had already been adjudged in an effective instrument of that court to bear contractual liability for repayment and should no longer bear tort liability was not improper. In fact, at the time of the ex post facto mortgage between Huada Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch, Huada Decoration Factory had completely ceased production and was insolvent. When Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch signed the mortgage contract with Huada Decoration Factory, both the mortgaged real estate and land were appraised, and their values were far lower than the creditor's rights enjoyed by Everbright Bank. The legal consequence that Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch should bear for the invalid mortgage is to return the funds it obtained based on the priority compensation from the mortgage. Therefore, the original trial court's finding that there was no direct causal relationship between the mortgage act of Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch and Huada Decoration Factory and the inability to recover the loan under Everbright Bank's loan contract was not improper. Everbright Bank's claim that Agricultural Bank of China Qingshan Sub-branch should bear joint and several liability for compensation for its entire loss of creditor's rights lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Regarding the ground of appeal raised by Everbright Bank that Ziyou Road Office should bear liquidation liability for Huada Decoration Factory and assume civil liability with the liquidated property, this Court holds that, based on the facts found in this case, Huada Decoration Factory’s business license has been revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce. Ziyou Road Office also stated at trial that Huada Decoration Factory is currently in a state of automatic dissolution. Revocation of a business license is an administrative penalty imposed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce on an enterprise legal person that has violated national administrative regulations on industry and commerce. According to Article 40 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "When a legal person terminates, it shall carry out liquidation in accordance with the law and discontinue activities outside the scope of liquidation," Article 46, which provides that "When an enterprise legal person terminates, it shall apply to the registration authority for cancellation of registration and make an announcement," and Article 47, which provides that "When an enterprise legal person is dissolved, it shall establish a liquidation organization to carry out liquidation," an enterprise legal person whose business license is revoked shall carry out liquidation according to law, and only after completing the cancellation of registration with the industry and commerce authority shall the enterprise legal person be deemed to have ceased to exist. Article 59 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) provides that when an enterprise legal person is dissolved or revoked, its competent authority shall organize a liquidation team to carry out liquidation. Huada Decoration Factory is a collectively-owned enterprise that has not undergone restructuring. Due to poor management, it ceased production since 1998. Under the circumstances where its business license has been revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce and the enterprise is in a state of dissolution, Ziyou Road Office, as the current competent authority of Huada Decoration Factory, shall carry out liquidation in accordance with the law. In this case, although Everbright Bank filed a tort action, it also raised a claim that Ziyou Road Office should bear liquidation liability for Huada Decoration Factory. According to the joinder of actions principle in the Civil Procedure Law and the principle of saving litigation costs for the parties, the issue of Ziyou Road Office's liquidation liability should be handled together in this case. Therefore, the ground of appeal raised by Everbright Bank that Ziyou Road Office should bear liquidation liability for Huada Decoration Factory and assume civil liability with the liquidated property complies with legal provisions, and this Court supports it. The original trial court's application of law was inappropriate and should be corrected.

In summary, the facts found by the original trial court are basically clear, but the application of law in some parts is inappropriate and should be corrected. In accordance with Articles 40, 46, and 47 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 59 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. The Civil Judgment (2007) Nei Min Er Chu Zi No. 21 of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region High People's Court is hereby vacated;

2. The claims of China Everbright Bank against Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding Decoration Factory and Agricultural Bank of China Baotou Qingshan Sub-branch are hereby dismissed;

3. The Ziyou Road Office of Qingshan District People's Government of Baotou City shall carry out liquidation of Inner Mongolia Baotou Huada Joint Venture Bedding Decoration Factory and assume civil liability with the liquidated property.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 169,657.2 for the first instance shall be borne by China Everbright Bank in the amount of RMB 135,725.76 and by the Ziyou Road Office of Qingshan District People's Government of Baotou City in the amount of RMB 33,931.44. Court acceptance fee of RMB 169,657.2 for the second instance shall be borne by China Everbright Bank in the amount of RMB 135,725.76 and by the Ziyou Road Office of Qingshan District People's Government of Baotou City in the amount of RMB 33,931.44.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jin Jianfeng

Acting Judge: Yin Yuan

Acting Judge: Pan Yongfeng

April 23, 2009

Clerk: Bai Xue

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Jin Jianfeng, Senior Judge: Born in 1959, Doctor of Laws, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 1998.
